note: Survey feet (HABS CT-359, 1995): x runs north up the house, z east, y over the first floor. Spaces tile each level: the building's outline on the outer faces of its walls, rooms meeting on the partitions' centre lines. Roofs are given as an architect would give them: footprint, plate height at the wall line, pitch (rise per foot) and overhang per edge; everything else is generated (tools/building/arch.py) and checked (validate.py).

roofs.note: The main block north of the south-east gable: steep slopes from the west and north walls to the flat at 35.9 (roof plan, elevations), the north face meeting the flat on x 105.5 from its eave at 18.9 (north elevation); the east face runs on from the south part. No south slope: round the Texas deck the flat comes to the well, whose walls rise to it. Open over the deck, which its pavilion covers.
The main block along the east front: slopes from the east wall (19.3) and the north wall to the flat; its south face is the south-east gable own south slope (19.3, 1.491), down to the south wall.

One ridge at 43.3 the length of the main block, z 47.4 (south elevation's gable peak, the attic plan, section B-B); both slopes at the west elevation's pitch 1.515 from the cornice at 28.0 a foot out from the west wall; the east slope meets the flat at 35.9 on z 52.3 (the roof plan's line). Its ends are the south and north gables, their fronts standing out 3 and 5 ft over the balconies.
a wall dormer: the west wall rises through the long roof's cornice into it, a window either side of the chimney (west elevation: feet 30.9, peak 39.3)
the great south-east gable facing east: rakes from 19.3, peak 35.7 (east elevation)
the great north-east gable facing east: peak 35.7 (east elevation)

Seven arched windows under a low hipped roof, back into the main roof.
The Texas deck's roof: a pavilion on the deck's posts, its point at x 57.2, z 64.8 (roof plan), 37.1 (east elevation); its eaves at 34.7 reach the roof plan's octagon, 20.7 ft across flats.

An octagonal spire over the alcove's deck, centred where the roof plan and section A-A put its point (x 73.2, z 37.2, over the house's west wall), its eave octagon 17.4 ft across flats (roof plan); eave 33.2 and point 47.25 (the south elevation's mark, PEAK OF ROOF 47'-3"). Its inner half dies into the long roof in valleys.
